text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel hails breakthrough to lowest tax rates in last 50 years.
- Bonn free to apply for EU aid for its plan to slaughter British and Swiss cattle, EU agriculture commissioner says.
- Reform of public health insurance means less room for manoeuvre for individual funds.
- Insurers and trade unions criticise Waigel's tax plan but most of industry gives it a warm welcome.
- European court rules Turkish people who have worked in Germany for at least four years should have unsrestricted access to German labour market.
HANDELSBLATT
- Tax reform plan reduces tax burden by 30 billion marks.
- New telecommunications consortium spearheaded by Deutsche Bahn and Mannesmann to be called Arcor.
- Supervisory board approves new Daimler-Benz structure.
- Enron Corp of U.S. withdraws interest in buying Berlin utility company Bewag.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Many tax breaks to go as part of overall reform of tax system.
- Headquarters of DASA, aerospace arm of Daimler-Benz, to shed jobs.
- Daimler restructuring means management board of parent has greater control.
- Bundesbank misses M3 money supply target for 1996.
DIE WELT
- Plans for pensions in new tax reform provoke split in leadership of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU).
- Tax reform plans should reduce burden on companies.
- Government set to announce spending freeze for government departments on Tuesday.
- Retailers demand tougher measures to combat theft.
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
